newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-BHP rules out gov't aid for steel.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-BHP rules out gov't aid for steel.

text.p: The Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd (BHP) has ruled out seeking government aid to assist its ailing steel division, incoming chairman Jerry Ellis, said on Sunday.
Ellis said the likelihood of Australia's largest industrial company seeking the sort of financial aid it did in the 1980s was "less likely than more likely."
BHP has announced its steel operations are under review in an effort to cut costs and improve operations, particularly at the Newcastle steelworks in New South Wales state.

Speaking on the Channel Nine Network Business Sunday television programme, Ellis said the government aid BHP received in the 1980s was "in the order of A$70 million to A$80 million" and provided the company with the confidence to invest more than A$1 billion.
In the most recent financial quarter ended August 1, the steel division's profits slumped to A$90 million from A$146 million in the previous corresponding period.
The fall in profits has been linked by BHP to weak international markets for its steel products and a strong Australian dollar, which undermines its revenues from exports.

Ellis, formerly head of BHP's minerals division, also said that BHP's US$2.4 billion acquisition of Magma Copper Co of the U.S. in January was a smart buy because it provides refining and smelting capacity in the world's largest copper market.
Long-term gains in copper should outweigh any short-term negatives brought on by the recent collapse in international copper prices, Ellis said.
He acknowledged, however, that "the jury might be out on whether the judgement was sound or not.
